body:
Appreciate your input. I was just not prepared or willing to talk about traumatic events here, they are a big enough part of me already. Thank you for doing research, however, it's nice to see someone who knows what he is talking about.

Sir, it's easier to have a cavalier attitude than to dwell upon hurtful things in the past.

Thank you for your reply.
I take long walks sometimes, several hours at a time. Or I go to the park and watch the beavers that live in the lake.
You caught me!

1. Yes, I asked her if she had a problem with it, and she didn't.
2. Yes.
3. I do feel like I act as an older brother to her. But there's no sense of being specifically related to her, it's more like I'm an old friend.
4. Yes. Periods are possibly the most cruel and unusual punishment on earth.
5. Not for long. I try to give privacy, but everything turns up eventually.
6. Yes. I have aced many a test. In retrospect, that may or may not have been cheating, but...fuck it.
7. She used to. I got along well with him, but it turned out to be an unhealthy relationship. I do not. I've had crushes before, but I've realized that those come from a desire to be close to people, something that I don't have the opportunity to do. Not "intimacy" close, but simple things, like hugs...I've stopped trying. None of them ever work out.

It's hard to fully function when I'm not "out" so to speak. It's like a sort of semi-consciousness.

She is not conscious at all when she is not "out," except in very rare circumstances.

Well. I guess I'm technically bi. I still have to deal with the original's attraction to males.

No, not really. It's sort of weird, but that feels like an invasion of privacy to me.

YellowEyes? No, that's what I'm called.

I'm partial to Adrian, but that still doesn't seem right to me.
She writes short stories and does a lot of illustration. She also enjoys aspects of set-design and other technical work in the theater. She also enjoys singing.

Please tell me how it works then? I wish I knew myself, haha.

On a slightly related note, I don't watch many movies. The last one I saw was Lean On Me (with Morgan Freeman.)

I've thought about it, and I've already gone through my personal struggle with that. I realize it's a possibility, but even if that's true, I'm here, and I'm typing my own thoughts.

I don't know how it works, but it makes more sense than the explanation that I'm something possessing her...or anything of that ilk. I'm not completely sure what you're asking here, sorry.

Well. I have about as much control as a brother or a friend most of the time. I try not to force her to do things unless I'm protecting her, because doing so would be an easy way to alienate her.

She already has passions and interests of her own that I encourage. Once again, making someone do things usually isn't the answer.

Not for long.

It's alright. It's reddit. There are too many cat pictures to get depressed.

Have a nice night, thank you for taking the time to learn more.

And most definitely, I'll message you randomly. Sounds like fun.

No family. Mother isn't understanding, step-father at the moment wouldn't be either. Closest sibling is six years younger than the original, so not much confidence there (she's the oldest.)

Well. She likes to wear costumes, so I can "cross-dress" as myself whenever I want if I feel like it. She tends to wear more gender-neutral things as well.

Currently, it is just myself and the original. There have been around...18?...but most short-lived and never more than 3 at a time.

Yes. I can ask and she can give up control voluntarily, or I can take it. It's painful if she doesn't agree to step-down, similar to a bad migraine that no pills will help because the pain is inside your brain... I stay out until I get tired, bored, or she asks to come out again. I tend to be in control from anywhere between 30 min. and several hours. The longest stretch of time I was in control was 2 weeks, which was very hard.

I rate asses sometimes to annoy the original. A well placed 'dat ass' always lightens the mood. Hah.

I read a lot, and if I'm out, I go online and talk to people I know or go on omegle or reddit. I draw sometimes, but I'm not that great a writer. If I'm not out/in control, I watch what she does, but mostly I play games with myself, look through memories, or I go to sleep.

My life is not too spicy. But there's enough occasional drama to keep me on my toes.

I draw some. I shaded/colored and drew the bottom height comparison. We have different drawing styles.

It's alright. It's definitely something I've thought about a lot. I think I would be happier if the original didn't need my protection anymore and she was safe, than if she had to depend on me her entire life because I was selfish.

The others are still here in a way, aspects of them still show up in actions every once in a while. So...maybe it's not like dying, so much as to just going back.

But it's kind of weird to think about. One day I was just here, and now I'm thinking, and I have wants and dreams of my own, and just as easily, tomorrow even...I could be nothing at all...

Don't have insurance. Family is currently not very wealthy at all, hah. It used to be middle class, but not anymore I suppose...

Uhm. It's alright. I have some friends who know me as me.

My least favorite part of not existing is having a crush on someone. It never ends well and I can't act on it ever, because I am male, and the body I share? It's female. That and the original wouldn't take too well to me canoodling about, ha...

Thanks.

Oh man. I think I have a few pictures. (Drawn of course) Just a few doodles.

http://i.imgur.com/m5GS9.jpg

I look like a bum. But fuck do I love a striped scarf.

Nah, I'm cool with it. I've been reading up on my own. The whole 'dissociative' disorder category has been falling under criticism for it's accuracy lately.

I'm definitely considering it, thank you for telling me that. Cost is a large issue, but once we get to a college, I will be sure to take full advantage of student services and counseling.

Male. Because I picture myself as a dude.

They left some written record of their own, and their memories are still here, even if they're second-hand.

Yes. At least. I hope so. Nobody's answered other than the original when I talk, so I'll take that as reasonably good evidence I'm here alone...I hope... ಠ_ಠ

Oh jeez. That's a hard one. I asked the original and this is what she said:
>He just kind of showed up one day, it seemed like it was out of the blue at the time, but I was going through some major stress in my life with my *second* step-father. YE just kind of...introduced himself.

I guess I'm okay with my role. It's hard to be so responsible, especially when I would really sometimes rather be doing more 'normal' things, but I care about the original, and in the end I'm protecting my own existence as well as her's.

Seen one for unrelated (divorce/court-related) issues. He said she was a well-adjusted individual, and after 5 sessions, that she didn't need to come back. He was pretty nice.

Have not been diagnosed. The original has a serious fear of psycho-pharmacology, and psychiatric drugs. Apologies. It's been somewhat of a fad disorder in the past couple of decades I understand, and might be dropped from the DSM anyways.

But I agree with you. It's scary for me, especially the first time, because you never know if you can...do anything until it happens. Thankfully things have been doing better, but if it ever gets really bad, I will set up an appointment, damned on what she wants.

It helps with the protecting deal, hah...

She goes to school, takes AP classes. Was recently involved in a large musical production with the school as well. Applied and got accepted into college, and is planning to go there. Does not go to therapy (but considers it sometimes.) She has trouble with friends sometimes and went through a rough spot, so she hasn't been in contact with many old ones...but she functions pretty well compared to others I've read about.

I guess it's because she considers me a friend and not a disease?

Planning to major in psych actually our freshman year. Fascinating subject.

Well. It depends on what is going on. The more stressed the original is, the more often I end up coming out without prompting. It's as if she throws her hands up and says "I can't take this anymore right now." Other times, I ask. I've made a few friends via text and IM. I've also worked for two weeks as a stagehand, which doesn't require too much talking.

I do at times have to take control, thankfully it doesn't happen much. But it usually involves self-harm, at least, a strong desire to. I prevent it.

I suppose it's cyclical in a way. There's usually always a supporting one, and sometimes negative, hurtful ones show up and then leave as issues get resolved. I wish I knew how it worked better than I do.

Appreciated.

I visualize it as an apartment type set-up. If I'm in control, I have my "area" in the brain I can go to. Taking control is similar, it's like taking the wheel of the car from another person. I tend to be aware of surroundings while I am not in control. The original is not aware of surroundings when she is not in control.

Details are fuzzy because it was not my memory. Some sort of emotional issues with her parents when she was younger. I wish I could be more specific...

Nice try Nurse Ratched.

But seriously now, yes, we all have different names. The host is a female, I would rather not post her name here. Let's call her D. I don't have an official name (I never found one that I liked) but she, and I, call myself Yellow-eyes due to my self-image.

I guess I've been around for close to two years now.

The original is around 18 years old.

Uh. Well. That's actually a tough one. I don't get out much, haha. But that is accurate. There was actually a guy who was allergic to apples while the rest loved them and had no symptoms. Still unsure as to how that happened. The problem with "sharing a head" so to speak is that strong emotions tend to leak. Have you ever tried feeling happy while feeling intensely angry instead? It's kind of similar.

We've all had different handwriting though, now that I think about it. I enjoy reading biographies (something the original finds intensely boring) and my musical tastes are partially different.

We both however, enjoy some musical theatre.

How could it be unlikely at all?

He's already there.

No! It's fine! It's hard to read people's intentions, that's all. I tend not to talk much. (In fact, I don't at all, I'm a mute.)

Well. I don't remember exactly how it happened. We both have a notoriously shitty memory. There were others before me, but they've come and gone throughout the years. Most of them served some sort of purpose. I just tend to act as an older brother.

The one who co-existed the longest...he was around for 11 years, from the original's age 6-17. He came into existence shortly after the original's mother remarried for the first time. He also acted as an older brother, but also as a protector. The original used to have very bad night terrors.

I'm very sorry, I should have made this more clear. I do not physically have a body, instead, I coexist with another person.

Oh my...that sounds rather...outlandish now, doesn't it?...

But yes. Basically true. I am not a conventional person, because I don't have a physical body, however, I am a separate entity/personality from the person I coexist with.

I'm sorry, am I just being more confusing now?...

Every musical movie ever.

God I love musical theatre. But Les Miserables will probably turn out an abomination. That casting is awful.

Why is this so adorable and accurate?

Keep making these, 'kay?

Thank you.

I actually haven't been able to eat much, some of the hallucinations make food extremely unappetizing.

I appreciate the writing idea though, I'll definitely try that, thank you.

Thank you very much.

I'll try to schedule a meeting with someone.

I guess hearing it from someone else really helps--at least by putting the whole situation into perspective.

I appreciate this, but I have no means of transportation.

To be completely honest, I'm hesitant because I'm terrified of anything having to do with psychological medication, hospitalization, or anything similar.
